analysis.one_line_summary: A creator shares step-by-step tutorial tips on achieving a voluminous at-home blowout using the Wavytalk Blowout Boost thermal brush.
analysis.full_description: A creator starts by showing a mirror selfie clip of her voluminous blowout that prompted questions on her social media story. She then transitions to showing her natural curly/wavy hair before demonstrating how she styles it section by section using the light blue Wavytalk Blowout Boost thermal brush. She provides practical tips: applying tension, doing one pass to smooth and a second to shape, wrapping around the handle for tighter curls, holding the brush at an angle to avoid tangling, and brushing out the final curls with fingers for full volume.

analysis.transcript_full_original: I posted this video on my story and a lot of you have asked me how I do my blowouts. So I'm going to show you what I use and some tips on how to get your hair to look like that. So first, I start off by completely detangling my hair. And then I go in with this Blowout Boost by Wavytalk. It's a thermal brush so it doesn't blow out any air, it just heats up like a curling iron. So in order to ensure you get the best results from this brush, you want to make sure that you're holding the section and pulling down with a lot of tension. In the front I like to do one pass to smooth it out, and then another pass to curl it and shape it to my face. I also find that wrapping it around the handle also makes it a little bit of a tighter curl. The best way to not get your hair tangled on the brush is to make sure you're holding it at an angle so that it slides through your hair instead of completely just wrap around the brush. I prefer to do curls at the end of each one because I feel like it adds a lot more volume, and volume is definitely something that I love for my hair. Once you're done, it should look like this. I personally prefer to run my hands through it and smooth it out a little bit, so you still get that volume and a little bit less of a curl. Just try it out and let me know what you think.
